reasons: Tests the key rules directly: late data, corrections, and unlicensed sources.
Uses a real database and a clean reset before running.
Each test has a clear expected answer.

terms.meaning: Tracking two times for each record: when it happened, and when the app learned about it.
Using information that was not known yet, which makes a view look better or more accurate than it really was.
The chosen moment at which the app is pretending to look.
One recorded event in a match, such as a ball, here stored with its timestamps and source.
Replace an earlier record with a corrected one, while keeping the original.

sections.name: File setup, start
sections.title: Sets up test event in database
sections.what: Sets a fixed start time for the test event and loads the database and helper functions that the tests need.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed start time makes every timestamp in the tests predictable.
sections.watch_out: The reset helper clears test data before setup, so these tests must never point at a database that holds real data.

sections.name: sec
sections.title: Converts seconds into timestamps
sections.what: Turns a number of seconds into a timestamp counted from the test event's start time.
sections.why: Likely reason: it lets tests write cutoffs as simple second counts, which is easier to read.
sections.watch_out: All times are relative to the start, so changing the start time shifts every cutoff in the tests together.

sections.name: ball
sections.title: Creates a test ball record
sections.what: Stores one ball record in the test database, with chosen runs or a wicket and a chosen delay between when it happened and when it was observed.
sections.why: Likely reason: it lets each test add late or odd records cheaply without repeating the full setup.
sections.watch_out: Each record gets a random source reference, so duplicate-record checks elsewhere will not catch these test records.

sections.name: bitemporal reads and leakage
sections.title: Checks reads ignore future and unlicensed data
sections.what: Checks that the match state at a cutoff counts only balls that happened and were seen by then. Checks that late-arriving balls are ignored, that a correction applies only from when it was seen, and that records from unlicensed sources are left out.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app must show only what was known at the chosen moment, and must only show data it has rights to display.
sections.watch_out: Event time and observed time are different. Mixing them up would let future information leak into a past view.

summary: Tests that the app's match-state view only uses information that was actually known at a chosen time, so it cannot accidentally show the future.
purpose: Protects against data leaks, where a view at one time uses balls that happened or were recorded later.
why: Likely reason: a replay or prediction that sees the future is misleading and would break the fairness of fan calls.
how: Before the tests, it resets the test database and creates a competition, season and event, then adds four synthetic balls with delayed observation times. Each test then reads the match state at a chosen cutoff. It checks that balls seen after the cutoff are ignored, that a correction only applies from when it was seen, and that unlicensed sources are left out.
inputs: Synthetic incidents in the test database with two timestamps each: when the event happened and when it was observed.
outputs: Pass or fail results. The tests write to the test database and clear it before the run.
risks: The tests write real rows to whatever database they point at, so pointing them at a real database would damage its data. Timing mistakes in the test setup would hide real leaks.
debug: If a test fails, check the cutoff time it uses and the observed time of the record. Look at the function that reads the state at a cutoff and confirm it filters on observed time, not only on event time.
